answer: Each agent can earn only one membership credential by locking a scarce token in a vault, with the lock recorded on-chain and released only after a long, public exit delay. The same credential signs its actions, so creating extra identities does not create extra voting weight or rewards. An attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens for each additional credential, paying opportunity cost and risking losses if the protocol slashes provable misconduct; names like juniper and onyx add no weight on their own.
